descriptor.scene: There is no human being anywhere in this frame. THREE OR MORE figures fill the middle of the frame from the waist up and are the subject: a small gathering of factory managers, every one of them the same one design, a small blocky luminous plum-glowing mascot in a cream newsboy cap, and among them ONE tiny inspector who is plainly SMALLER and DIMMER and BARE-HEADED with no cap or hat of any kind, still holding his small brass lamp. The camera is nearer than an establishing view and every figure reads clearly. The managers are gathered in a warm half-circle around the tiny inspector, who stands on a low wooden crate at the centre so he is level with them; mitten arms are raised toward him in an easy salute. The mood is warm and glad, a send-off and not a funeral, nobody sad and nobody solemn. Behind and above them, present but never competing: a brand-new machine has arrived on the factory floor, a big clean cream-and-brass engine still half-wrapped in pale cloth, a wooden crate lid leaning against it and a pale canvas parachute settling in soft folds behind it; and at the LEFT, a run of old pale scaffolding is coming down, its poles already half-stacked in a neat pile on the floor. Warm honeyed daylight and plum glow. Composition: the half-circle and the inspector fill the middle, the new machine behind at the right, the stacked scaffolding at the left; the upper left stays calm warm wall.
